questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Famous stories about mermaids and sea monsters
Plans for underwater homes and their problems
How to train to become a professional deep-sea diver
Why fish are disappearing from the world's oceans
questions.why: Neil says they'll hear about projects to create liveable underwater habitats and their challenges.

options: A small submarine that takes tourists to the seabed
An underwater amusement park for families only
A research station where divers train for jobs
A huge see-through globe attached to the seabed
questions.why: Neil describes it as a huge transparent globe attached to the seabed.

questions.q: How many people could live in Ocean Spiral?
options: Five thousand
Five hundred
Fifty thousand
Seventy-three
questions.why: Rob says it would have space for five thousand underwater residents.

questions.q: According to engineer Masaki Takeuchi, why was Ocean Spiral designed?
options: To give rich people a luxury place to go on holiday
To protect rare sea animals from fishing boats
To use the deep sea to help with food and energy
To give people a way to escape rising sea levels
questions.why: He says the world faces problems with food, energy and water, and they want to use the deep sea.

questions.q: How much of the Ocean Spiral project has been built so far?
options: Only the central tower
None of it
About half
All of it except the park
questions.why: Rob says it is still in the planning stages and no part has yet been built.

options: The Japanese engineer who designed Ocean Spiral
A science-fiction writer who writes about the sea
A doctor who treats divers with health problems
An ex-military diver with the underwater record
questions.why: He is an ex-military diver who set the 73-day record and heads The Aquarius.

questions.q: According to Roger Garcia, what happens to the body after a long time in The Aquarius?
options: People lose a lot of weight
People's eyesight gets worse
The body takes in more nitrogen
People cannot sleep
questions.why: He says at higher pressure you take on more nitrogen, and your voice may change a little.

questions.q: What causes the bends, according to Neil?
options: Returning to the surface too quickly
Breathing normal air underwater
Staying near the surface too long
Eating the wrong food before diving
questions.why: He says the bends is caused by nitrogen bubbles when returning to the surface too quickly.
